NAME: Merchant Category Spend in EUR
DESC:
A payment processor wants the card spend of the last month per merchant category, converted to euros. Transactions come from many acquirers that format merchant codes and currency codes inconsistently. Two small reference tables are available: the merchant catalog and the exchange rates.

Implement solve so that it returns the spend per merchant category.

Input

transactions_df (very large)

column type description
txn_id string unique, never null
merchant_code string dirty merchant code, e.g. " m-001 ", "M001", "m_001"; may be null
amount string decimal text in the transaction currency; negative for a refund; may be null
currency string ISO code with arbitrary case and spaces, e.g. " eur"

merchants_df (small, at most 10^4 rows)

column type description
merchant_code string dirty merchant code
merchant_name string display name
category string clean lowercase category, never null

fx_df (small, at most 200 rows)

column type description
currency string ISO code with arbitrary case and spaces; unique after normalization
rate_to_eur double value of 1 unit of the currency in EUR

Rules

  1. A merchant code is normalized by converting it to uppercase and removing every character that is not a letter A-Z or a digit 0-9: " m-001 ", "M001" and "m_001" all become "M001". The same normalization applies to both transactions_df and merchants_df. A code that is null or empty after normalization never matches anything.
  2. merchants_df may list the same merchant several times under different spellings. All spellings of a merchant have the same category.
  3. A currency code is normalized by trimming spaces and converting to uppercase, in both transactions_df and fx_df.
  4. A transaction is excluded if its amount is null, if its merchant is not in merchants_df, or if its currency is not in fx_df.
  5. amount_eur = amount * rate_to_eur. Refunds (negative amounts) are included as they are.
  6. Both joins with the reference tables must be broadcast joins. The grader disables automatic broadcasting (spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold=-1), and one hidden test inspects the physical plan.

Output

A DataFrame with one row per category that has at least one counted transaction, with exactly these columns, in this order:

column type description
category string
txn_count long number of counted transactions
total_eur double sum of amount_eur, rounded to 2 decimals
avg_eur double average of amount_eur, rounded to 2 decimals

Rows are sorted by total_eur descending, then category ascending.

transactions_df

txn_id merchant_code amount currency
T1 " m-001 " "100.00" "eur"
T2 "M001" "50.00" "MAD"
T3 "m_002" "20.00" "USD"
T4 "M-003" "10.00" "EUR"
T5 "M002" null "EUR"
T6 "M 002" "30.00" "GBP"
T7 "M-004" "40.00" " eur"

merchants_df

"M-001" Marjane Anfa grocery
"m001" Marjane Anfa (old) grocery

fashion 1 18.4 18.4

Function signature

from pyspark.sql import DataFrame

def solve(transactions_df: DataFrame, merchants_df: DataFrame, fx_df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
    ...

Constraints

  • Use the PySpark DataFrame API. Do not convert to pandas, do not call collect() or toPandas() inside solve, and do not use Python UDFs.
  • transactions_df has up to 10^9 rows.
  • The returned DataFrame may be empty; its columns and types must still match the specification.

SOLUTION:
from pyspark.sql import DataFrame
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def normalize_code(col):
    # Majuscules puis suppression de tout ce qui n'est ni lettre ni chiffre : " m-001 " -> "M001".
    return F.regexp_replace(F.upper(col), "[^A-Z0-9]", "")


def solve(transactions_df: DataFrame, merchants_df: DataFrame, fx_df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
    # 1. Petites tables de référence : clé normalisée, clés vides exclues, UNE ligne par clé
    #    (sinon la jointure multiplie les transactions).
    merchants = (
        merchants_df
        .select(normalize_code(F.col("merchant_code")).alias("merchant_key"), "category")
        .filter(F.col("merchant_key").isNotNull() & (F.col("merchant_key") != ""))
        .dropDuplicates(["merchant_key"])
    )
    fx = fx_df.select(F.upper(F.trim(F.col("currency"))).alias("currency_key"), "rate_to_eur")

    # 2. Grande table : mêmes normalisations, montant en double, montants null exclus.
    txns = (
        transactions_df
        .withColumn("merchant_key", normalize_code(F.col("merchant_code")))
        .withColumn("currency_key", F.upper(F.trim(F.col("currency"))))
        .withColumn("amount", F.col("amount").cast("double"))
        .filter(F.col("amount").isNotNull())
    )

    # 3. Deux broadcast joins (inner : marchand ou devise inconnus => transaction exclue).
    joined = (
        txns
        .join(F.broadcast(merchants), on="merchant_key", how="inner")
        .join(F.broadcast(fx), on="currency_key", how="inner")
        .withColumn("amount_eur", F.col("amount") * F.col("rate_to_eur"))
    )

    return (
        joined.groupBy("category")
        .agg(
            F.count(F.lit(1)).alias("txn_count"),
            F.round(F.sum("amount_eur"), 2).alias("total_eur"),
            F.round(F.avg("amount_eur"), 2).alias("avg_eur"),
        )
        .orderBy(F.col("total_eur").desc(), F.col("category").asc())
    )
